paragraphs: Walk bank-$8F condition functions starting eleven bytes after the room header.
Each function word is followed by that condition's own payload; X points at
the payload when the function runs. PEA supplies an RTS return to the loop.
A failed condition advances X past its payload and returns with RTS. A match
jumps to Use_StatePointer_inX, which drops that near return and exits with RTL.
X is the chosen state-header address, not the address of a pointer to dereference.
The default condition reaches this routine with X immediately after its own
function word, at the inline default state header. Matching non-default checks
instead load X from their payload's state pointer. Discard the scan loop's
two-byte return before RTL returns to the selector's long caller.
This condition's payload is one event byte followed by a two-byte state pointer.
On success select that pointed-to state through the common long-return exit.
On failure skip all three payload bytes and RTS back to the condition scan.
State offset $18 is an optional bank-$8F setup callback. A zero word skips it;
otherwise JSR invokes the setup routine, which returns with RTS. Restore the
saved data bank and processor status before RTL returns to the long caller.
This wrapper expects the state-header data to be readable in the entry data bank.
Read the optional door-ASM word from bank-$83 door data, but execute it in
bank $8F. For a nonzero pointer, PEA builds the callback's near RTS return
before the indirect JMP. The wrapper then restores bank/status and returns
with RTL. This is distinct from the room-state setup and main callbacks.
Execute the cached bank-$8F room-main word pointer when it is nonzero.
Set X to zero for the indexed indirect JSR, and restore the caller's data bank
after the callback's RTS. Unlike setup/door wrappers, this entry has no PHP/PLP
or register-width setup; it relies on the calling gameplay path's register mode.

lines.comment: Start from the room-header address supplied in X.
Add the fixed header length without an incoming carry.
Skip eleven header bytes to the first condition-function word.
Use X as the condition-stream cursor.
Read the next bank-$8F condition function's word address.
Save the callback word for the indirect near jump.
Advance past the two-byte function word to its payload.
Supply a synthetic RTS return to the loop, not a new long-call frame.
Run the condition function; failure returns here via RTS.
Select the state header at X itself, not a pointer read from [X].
Discard the condition loop's synthetic near return word.
Return directly to the caller of Room_State_Checking_Handler.
Read the event byte at the current condition payload.
Discard the neighboring state-pointer byte.
Test this event against the game's event flags.
On failure, skip this condition's payload and return to the stream loop.
On success, read the state pointer immediately after the event byte.
Use that selected state-header address as X.
Take the shared success exit, which discards the synthetic near return.
Skip the event byte and two-byte state pointer on the failure path.
RTS resumes the condition loop at its next function word.
Use the room state chosen by the condition stream.
Read the setup-ASM pointer at state offset $18.
A zero pointer means there is no setup callback.
Select this code bank for the optional room callback.
Call the bank-$8F setup routine with a near RTS return.
Restore the data bank saved before the callback.
Restore the saved processor status.
Return to the long caller after optional setup ASM.
Use the current door-header pointer.
Read the door-ASM word from bank-$83 door data.
Skip the callback when its pointer is zero.
Use a scratch word for the indirect near jump.
Select bank $8F for executing door ASM.
Create the near return word minus one expected by the callback's RTS.
Jump to the bank-$8F door callback through the scratch pointer.
Restore the caller's data bank after the optional callback.
Restore the processor status saved on entry.
Return to the long caller, not directly from the door callback.
Read the room-main callback pointer cached from the state header.
Zero skips the per-update room callback.
Preserve the caller's data bank around the room-main routine.
Use bank $8F for the room-main callback's data accesses.
Use X = 0 to call through the pointer without an added index.
Call bank-$8F room main ASM using its cached word pointer.
Restore the data bank before returning to gameplay.
Return to the caller; this wrapper does not save processor status.
